video_title: Los Angeles Clippers 2026 Offseason Part 1: Kawhi future, Aspiration, & more | Third Apron Podcast

quotes.speaker: Law Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers' 2025-26 season was a nightmare with complex offseason ahead
quotes.excerpt: This season was a nightmare in a lot of ways for a lot of people.
quotes.quote: This season was a nightmare in a lot of ways for a lot of people. Like, you know, this was the first season where you put a word on social media and you get dirty looks. I knew from the Clippers standpoint that it was going to be complicated September 1. That was before the bad basketball set in. I think they had a good season in terms of just getting to that 42-win mark. That was their accomplishment. And even that accomplishment was rooted in initial failure, and then they failed again by putting themselves in position to make the playoffs just to smoke a fourth-quarter lead in a Play-In Tournament game against a team that lost 45 games and still didn't make the playoffs either. That's just going out sad. It makes this offseason incredibly intriguing because they have everything going on. You want to talk about second-round pick? They got one of those, they got two of those. You want to talk about a lottery pick? Holy crap, they have the fifth pick in the draft because of trades that they made during the season. You want to talk about restricted free agency, unrestricted free agency, player options, team options, injured dudes. You have that. And none of that involves Kawhi Leonard, who is, you know, the league is still investigating the Aspiration scandal. I hope we can use that word. I know sometimes you say that word in the most objective sense and people want to know why you're using that word. So, it's been a weird year, it's been a very difficult year covering them, and they have things to be excited for, but they also have things to be wary of. Pretty commonplace for a team smack dab in the middle of the West.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Aspiration scandal's potential impact on Clippers' future and draft picks
quotes.excerpt: That Aspiration scandal probably the worst organizational kind of situation since I want to say the Suns.
quotes.quote: I'm really impressed with the work they did. That Aspiration scandal probably the worst organizational kind of situation since I want to say the Suns had that toxic workplace environment thing four years ago. That led to a sale. I don't think that's going to happen with the Clippers. But it just we still so much uncertainty and we still need to touch on it because it's going to hang over what they might be able to do, what they might not be able to do. And it doesn't seem like we're close. I don't know if we're close to getting anything done. The most recent update was a month ago, one of the co-founders of Aspiration is now cooperating with one of the lead attorneys investigating everything. So we'll see what happens, if it happens before free agency, maybe even after, but that that's going to be significant because we could be looking at what if the Clippers lose several first-round picks? What if it leads to somehow Kawhi not being able to be on the roster? So, if one of the worst-case scenarios happens, what do you still do you see them do you see that kind of changing their direction or do you think they're still going to kind of push towards the same kind of direction they've been heading, just trying to be as good as possible?

quotes.speaker: Law Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers' competitive stance and offseason financial uncertainty with Kawhi
quotes.excerpt: The owner in place has always tried to be competitive. They don't have the draft assets to be anything otherwise.
quotes.quote: The owner in place has always tried to be competitive. They don't have the draft assets to be anything otherwise. Their floor has to be where it is. And plus the front office has been in place for a while now, almost a decade. The head coach has been in place for one of he's got one of the longest consecutive tenures now in the league. They have win now personnel up and down between ownership, front office, and the coaching. Their star player is in his mid-30s and I consider him year-to-year at this point, even if those years are elite. If the same decision-makers are in place, then I expect the outlook to remain the same. There's no incentive for them to have otherwise. And that's what you're talking about here. If the principals are still running the team and making the decisions, there aren't any suspensions or expulsions or anything like that, then I don't expect changes. If there are, you got to see who's there. You got to see what's left. You got to see what they have to say. There's a lot of 'we'll see' involved with that. It's a lot of uncertainty. I can't imagine it being a non-factor for this offseason. They can say it was a non-factor during the season. I actually believe them. Look at how the season went. I talk to coaches and players all the time. Their focus is winning basketball games, not looking at pocketbooks. But the offseason is about looking at pocketbooks. There's so much uncertainty and until there are definitive conclusions and consequences, you have to kind of operate status quo going forward.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers' trade deadline moves hint at hedging against Aspiration penalties
quotes.excerpt: I do wonder though if what they did in the trade deadline is maybe an indication of them wanting to go a little younger.
quotes.quote: I do wonder though if what they did in the trade deadline is maybe an indication of them wanting to go a little younger and maybe they will maybe they will be open to doing that. And maybe an even an indication that they sense, hey, maybe the hammer is coming. Maybe we we need to start hedging in case we do get penalized. Because obviously the Harden trade doesn't seem like that was really up to them. That was mostly him wanting to get somewhere where he could probably get a little better contract. And but maybe also the investigation, maybe he felt like that also could have impacted his negotiations with the Clippers. Then there's the Zubac trade, which in my opinion, was an opportunity they just couldn't refuse. Even if they didn't keep the fifth pick, getting two distant first-round picks is really critical, especially because of the uncertainty of whether they're going to keep these picks or not. And then overall, I just I love the turnaround they did. Going from the oldest team in the league, oldest rotation, one of the oldest rotations, like in terms of the actual players they were expected to play on a nightly basis in history, to getting Garland, Zubac, Bennedict Mathurin. I really love the turnaround. I love the work they did. I came out really impressed with the work they did, their negotiations.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Suggesting trading Kawhi Leonard due to age, injury, and team's capped ceiling
quotes.excerpt: I'd probably just lean further and trade Kawhi Leonard anyways. I just feel that with everything the Clippers have going against them.
quotes.quote: In my opinion, if I were them, I'd probably just lean further and trade Kawhi Leonard anyways. I just because one, as amazing as he was, yes, he's he's about to turn 35, maybe he plays even fewer games. I just feel that with the all the everything the Clippers have going against them, all these disadvantages that they've got right now, with their draft pick situation, I think there's probably going to be good, but I think their ceiling's kind of capped. And that I feel like whether they keep him or whether they trade him for some veterans, draft picks, I feel like they're still kind of like trending towards mostly being in the Play-In range, maybe slightly above that. In which case, I would probably act earlier, see what I see what you could get for Leonard now. Maybe you could push back maybe you want to push back on like as far as their ceiling, but I feel like they're heading towards the same type of outcome for the next few seasons anyways, with or without him.

quotes.speaker: Law Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard's personal decision-making regarding his future with the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: Kawhi Leonard has to determine what he wants for himself. Does he feel like there's a team out there that he want to play with?
quotes.quote: I think that's a challenging part. I think Kawhi Leonard has to determine what he wants for himself. Does he feel like a team there's a team out there that he want to play with? But at this stage of his career, Kawhi has these relationships here, he's from here. He has a level of pride in this organization that it's not like you're talking about a lot of other dudes, right? So he could easily re-up and say, hey, I'll play this out. And that could be a choice that he makes. Especially knowing that the Clippers, again, they're not in a tank situation. They're in a we're trying to be competitive and figure figure stuff out. It's like, is Kawhi cool with that? We got to we got to see, but you can see where he could possibly lean a little bit more towards trying to make it work rather than the alternative. Kawhi has seen his contemporaries and their efforts to do stuff and how that's worked out. James Harden, for example, shout out to him for getting to a point where his new team is in the Conference Finals. James's first Conference Finals in eight years. And it ain't going great, at least to start that series. Paul got a chance to be on a team that overcame a 3-1 deficit in the first round, just to get swept by the damn Knicks in, you know, the same team Harden is playing against now. Russell Westbrook, he ended the Clippers' season in 2025 and then sat out all free agency, hooked up with a Kings team that not only wound up being one of the worst in the league, one of the five, six lost teams, but wound up out of the top five in the draft as well. The grass isn't always greener.

quotes.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
quotes.summary_phrase: Limited trade return for Kawhi Leonard due to contract, age, injury, and market changes
quotes.excerpt: The biggest thing is for the Clippers, I don't think the returns are going to be particularly strong.
quotes.quote: He's going to have, if if a trade is on the table, he's going to have a lot of agency, a lot of say as far as where to go because he is on the last year of his contract. Whoever trades for him, if that happened, they could extend him. So that's going to he's going to be able to put his his thumb on the scale a little. The biggest thing is for the Clippers, I don't think the returns are going to be particularly strong. For several reasons. The obviously as for the factors I I relayed earlier, age, injury risk, that stuff. I think the the lottery reform, I've been talking about this in all my shows where I think teams are going to be less likely to trade as many draft picks as they have in recent years, at least for the time being. And especially it doesn't really apply to the Clippers, but maybe some of these teams out there, they don't have that many picks. Like, I don't know, the Warriors, for example, they're a team that kind of been linked to Kawhi. And that's more so I think just like as far as a fit, just like they can trade up to four firsts. And the reporting was they offered all that for Giannis. Are they still willing to offer quite that many for Giannis? And if and then what will that mean as far as an offer for Kawhi? So I I feel like the type of offer the Clippers could end up getting for Kawhi is kind of like similar to what the Suns got for KD. It's you get like a you get a good starter, a good young guy, and maybe like one really good draft pick. Maybe you can get a second really good draft pick just because the Clippers had just negotiated really well recently. Maybe they like after the Zubac trade, I I wonder if they can maybe they could really surprise me and get a lot more. So obviously with the trade market, it starts with Kawhi, I mean with Giannis. He's been linked to like the Warriors, I said, Miami. I think those teams make some sense for Kawhi as if they don't get Giannis. You can get like I mentioned some solid starters, up to four first from these teams. Just going through my list. Fit-wise, I like Minnesota for Kawhi, but they can only offer two picks, so that one's more of a long shot. I think Detroit on paper makes sense. And if you're the Clippers, you're probably hoping Detroit's interested if that means you could maybe get one of Jalen Duren or Ausar Thompson, but I think that's pretty unlikely. Houston, I saw they were linked potentially. They have a lot of nice players and picks. And then there's the Sixers where you're taking back a bad contract, you're taking back Paul George or Embiid, but maybe you get control of your picks back. Maybe you get the Sixers have the Clippers 2028 pick and 2029 swap. Maybe you could get control of that. That one I intrigues me. And then also kind of a long shot, there's like the there's the Lakers just because they have cap space. Maybe if there's a LeBron for Kawhi sign-and-trade. I I say it's unlikely, but it's the LeBron's best chance to get a lot of money. And then also the Clippers can have a replacement star. And then at the same time, you could also apply that with KD in Houston just in case they wanted to switch things up there.

quotes.speaker: Law Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard's health history and the risk for potential trade partners
quotes.excerpt: It is still a massive undertaking to acquire a player with his medical history and what he needs to be maintained.
quotes.quote: I honestly I just feel like, you know, when it comes to Kawhi, the other aspect is, even though he's I would say the healthiest that he's been since the 2010s. I I really don't want to overstate. He is remarkably healthy compared to what he's dealt with most of this decade. That said, it is still a massive undertaking to acquire a player with his medical history and what he needs to be maintained. Toronto did great for the year that they had him. Obviously, this is was the sticking point in San Antonio's breakdown in the relationship with Kawhi. I think the Clippers have had a great great like five or I mean, he's been with the team since 2019, but he tore his ACL and needed ACL surgery in 2021. And I mean, they've done a great job taking care of Kawhi, treating Kawhi for things that you we all were familiar with and things like the inflammation that we just were like, what is this and why is it afflicting him at that moment? That thing cost him his his best potential playoff team in 2024, a gold medal, you know, cost him a gold medal in 2024. Cost him the beginning of the Intuit Dome era. And now it's not a thing anymore. That's a big credit to the Clippers medical team and training team. And that's like, do you does a team feel that confident in their staff to acquire a player like that? And that is something that, look, I'm not going to pretend to be super well versed in that. I just see who misses games and how guys are when they get back across the league. I, you know, I don't have those kind of the insight. I just have WebMD. I have WebMD and and NBA injury reports. But that is a factor that again, is not always a factor when you're talking about acquiring certain guys in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Law Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers' critical need for point guards and passing ability
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers were dead last in the NBA in assists. Despite having a star point guard on the roster the entire season.

text_blocks.speaker: Law Murray
text_blocks.text: I don't love these dudes. They're so flawed. The Clippers were dead last in the NBA in assists. Despite having a star point guard on the roster the entire season. They were 30th. A lot of that comes from the lack of ball movement and depth at that position. When James was on the bench or when you trade James, you got to wait a month just to debut Darius, just to debut a player who had a minute restriction and a games restriction. That's tough. Chris Dunn had to handle the ball way more than he probably should. Kawhi had to handle the ball way more than he probably should. None of your frontcourt players are good passers, especially after you trade Zoo. They need passing. That needs to be a thing across positions, but they especially need it at guard. Benedict Mathurin was their backup point guard. That is ridiculous. In a spot in the draft where the best players are guards, that's where you start. But everyone who comes onto the team besides that, that is going to be the thing on your mind. The complication, you have a bunch of shooting guards that have a bunch of decisions in their contracts. Mathurin is restricted. Bogdan Bogdanovic has a team option. Bradley Beal is coming off of major surgery and has a player option that he has every reason to opt into because of said circumstances with his health. You have team options on Jordan Miller and Kobe Sanders. They're stretching that role. You need some true point guards, especially since you're handing the keys to Darius Garland, who again, star player, but a guy who you're going to have health concerns with for the rest of his current contract with the team.

text_blocks.speaker: Yossi Gozlan
text_blocks.text: You're right, they even if assuming they keep the fifth pick, even if they trade down a little bit, they'd still be in position to draft one of these top guards. I would probably think they should get yet another guard, some veteran guard in free agency, trade, because Garland, you got to factor in he might miss a good amount of time.

quotes.speaker: Law Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers' dire big man situation with injured Yannick and aging veterans
quotes.excerpt: You have no credible starter. The Clippers were an awful rebounding team this year. Awful on both ends.
quotes.quote: I couldn't be lower on all of those dudes. As far as like how you're starting next season, I think you have to safely assume that Yannick will not be ready to start the year. And because he's a young player who was, it was very upsetting to see him get hurt the way that he did because he was progressing rapidly. A Lisfranc might as well be an ACL or an Achilles as far as like getting back and everything. Yannick's not going to be ready to start the season. Brook Lopez is 38 years old. When he was brought in, it was with the idea that he'd be a backup and in a reduced role. They played Brook way too much. And not only was that hurtful for this end of this past season, it also means going into this season, how much does that take away from Brook? What does the decline look like? And then there's Isaiah, who tore his Achilles at the beginning of last season, then he suffers a high ankle sprain. He has no business starting. He's barely a decent backup. You have no credible starter. The Clippers were an awful rebounding team this year. Awful on both ends. You need to re-look at where your size is in the front court for sure.
